title: Operator Kantorovich inequality for 2-positive linear maps
statement:
Let $0<m\le A\le M$, and let $X,Y$ be partial isometries on a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ whose final spaces are orthogonal to each other. Let $\Phi$ be a $2$-positive linear map. **Operator Kantorovich inequality.** Then

$$
\left\\|\Phi(X^*AY)\Phi(Y^*AY)^{-1}\Phi(Y^*AX)\Phi(X^*AX)^{-1}\right\\|\le \left(\frac{M-m}{M+m}\right)^2.
$$

This assertion is motivated by the operator Wielandt inequality and related Schwarz inequalities for $2$-positive maps. The authors state that they have been unable to prove or disprove it, so its status remains open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5690

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2012).
source_name: Minghua Lin, “On an operator Kantorovich inequality for positive linear maps”, arXiv:1212.5690 (2012).
